title: "FRED-MD"

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
devtools::load_all()
library(tidyverse)
library(fbi)
library(psych)
library(kableExtra)
```

This chapter combines the four Labor-market series from [Unemployment](unemployment.qmd) with the three CPI subcomponents from [CPI Components](cpi-components.qmd) into one 7-series matrix, spanning two economic domains that have no obvious reason to comove:

- `MANEMP`: Manufacturing
- `DMANEMP`: Durable Goods
- `NDMANEMP`: Nondurable Goods
- `SRVPRD`: Service-Providing
- `CPIAPPSL`: Apparel
- `CPITRNSL`: Transportation
- `CPIMEDSL`: Medical Care

Manufacturing is still (approximately) the sum of Durable and Nondurable Goods, so that mechanical near-identity persists in this larger matrix. The question this chapter asks: does the joint diagonal test still correctly separate that one known real relationship from the six cross-domain (Labor vs. CPI) and near-independent within-domain pairs that surround it, once the matrix is no longer curated down to 3-4 series? As in the Unemployment chapter, every Diagonal subsection below also reports a "No Manufacturing" variant — the same joint test with Manufacturing dropped — to isolate how much of any rejection is that one mechanical relationship versus broader structure across the matrix.

```{R fredmd-load-data}
#| echo: false
#| message: false

fred_data <- fredmd(
  "../data/real-data/FRED-2026-05.csv",
  date_start = NULL, date_end = NULL, transform = FALSE
) |> as_tibble()

X_data <- fred_data |>
  select(date, MANEMP, DMANEMP, NDMANEMP, SRVPRD, CPIAPPSL, CPITRNSL, CPIMEDSL) |>
  drop_na() |>
  rename(
    Manufacturing = MANEMP,
    `Durable Goods` = DMANEMP,
    `Nondurable Goods` = NDMANEMP,
    Services = SRVPRD,
    Apparel = CPIAPPSL,
    Transportation = CPITRNSL,
    `Medical Care` = CPIMEDSL
  )

X_mat <- as.matrix(X_data[, -1])
```

`r nrow(X_data)` monthly observations, `r format(min(X_data$date))` to `r format(max(X_data$date))`.

```{R fredmd-helpers}
#| echo: false

# Null-restricted z-test (rho = 0): avoids assuming Gaussian k40/k04/k31/k13.
ece_pval_null <- function(X) {
  p <- ncol(X)
  pval_mat <- matrix(NA, p, p)
  colnames(pval_mat) <- rownames(pval_mat) <- colnames(X)
  for (i in 1:(p - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):p) {
      pair <- cbind(X[, i], X[, j])
      pval <- ece.test(pair, type = "z.test", kappa = ece.kappa(pair, rho = 0, method = "mom"), rho = 0)$p.value
      pval_mat[i, j] <- pval
      pval_mat[j, i] <- pval
    }
  }
  diag(pval_mat) <- 0
  pval_mat
}

# Bold any off-diagonal cell whose corresponding p-value is < 0.05.
bold_sig <- function(display_mat, pval_mat) {
  m   <- nrow(display_mat)
  out <- matrix("", m, m, dimnames = dimnames(display_mat))
  for (i in seq_len(m)) {
    for (j in seq_len(m)) {
      sig <- i != j && !is.na(pval_mat[i, j]) && pval_mat[i, j] < 0.05
      out[i, j] <- kableExtra::cell_spec(sprintf("%.3f", display_mat[i, j]), "html", bold = sig)
    }
  }
  out
}

# Per-series penalty search: choose pen.value so the segmentation-implied
# omega matches ECE's own segmentation-free estimate as closely as possible.
omega_match_penalty <- function(x, grid) {
  target <- ece.complexity(x, x)
  errs <- sapply(grid, function(pv) {
    seg       <- segment_mean_vec(x, penalty = "Manual", pen.value = pv)
    seg_omega <- lag_diff(seg, seg, k = 1) / length(x)
    abs(seg_omega - target) / abs(target)
  })
  grid[which.min(errs)]
}

fredmd_fit_segmentation <- function(X_mat, grid) {
  pen <- apply(X_mat, 2, omega_match_penalty, grid = grid)
  X_seg <- sapply(colnames(X_mat), function(cn) {
    segment_mean_vec(X_mat[, cn], penalty = "Manual", pen.value = pen[cn])
  })
  colnames(X_seg) <- colnames(X_mat)
  list(pen = pen, X_seg = X_seg)
}

fredmd_plot_series <- function(dates, X_mat, X_seg, title, ylab, zero_line = FALSE) {
  X_df <- bind_cols(
    date = dates, as.data.frame(X_mat),
    as.data.frame(X_seg) |> rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_segment"))
  )
  p <- X_df |>
    pivot_longer(cols = -date, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
    mutate(
      type   = if_else(str_ends(series, "_segment"), "Segmented", "Raw"),
      sector = str_remove(series, "_segment$")
    ) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = date, y = value, color = sector, group = series))
  if (zero_line) p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray")
  p +
    geom_line(aes(linewidth = type)) +
    scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(Raw = 0.4, Segmented = 1.0), guide = "none") +
    facet_wrap(~sector, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = ylab, color = "Sector", caption = "Source: FRED-MD") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
}

fredmd_plot_residuals <- function(dates, X_resid, title) {
  X_resid |>
    as_tibble() |>
    bind_cols(date = dates) |>
    pivot_longer(cols = -date, names_to = "sector", values_to = "value") |>
    ggplot(aes(x = date, y = value, color = sector)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) +
    facet_wrap(~sector, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = "Residual") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
}

fredmd_acf_naive <- function(X_resid) {
  par(mfrow = c(ncol(X_resid), 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))
  for (i in seq_len(ncol(X_resid))) {
    acf(X_resid[, i], main = "", xaxt = "n", ylab = colnames(X_resid)[i])
  }
  axis(1)
  mtext("Lag", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
}

fredmd_ece_terms <- function(X_mat, window) {
  cn  <- colnames(X_mat)
  idx <- combn(ncol(X_mat), 2)

  ece_cov <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(ncol(idx)), function(k) {
    i <- idx[1, k]
    j <- idx[2, k]
    s <- lag_term(X_mat[, i], X_mat[, j])
    tibble(t = seq_len(nrow(X_mat)), row = cn[i], col = cn[j], raw = s)
  })
  ece_var <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(ncol(X_mat)), function(i) {
    s <- lag_term(X_mat[, i], X_mat[, i])
    tibble(t = seq_len(nrow(X_mat)), row = cn[i], col = cn[i], raw = s)
  })
  bind_rows(ece_cov, ece_var) |>
    mutate(row = factor(row, levels = cn), col = factor(col, levels = cn)) |>
    group_by(row, col) |>
    mutate(run = rolling_mean(raw, window), global = mean(raw)) |>
    ungroup()
}

fredmd_plot_ece_trend <- function(terms_df) {
  ggplot(terms_df, aes(x = t)) +
    geom_line(aes(y = raw), color = "gray80") +
    geom_hline(aes(yintercept = global), linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
    geom_line(aes(y = run), color = "steelblue", na.rm = TRUE) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(row), cols = vars(col), scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "time", y = "ECE term (covariance scale)") +
    theme_minimal()
}

fredmd_kappa_table <- function(X_resid) {
  cn  <- colnames(X_resid)
  idx <- combn(ncol(X_resid), 2)
  purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(ncol(idx)), function(k) {
    i <- idx[1, k]
    j <- idx[2, k]
    kap <- ece.kappa(X_resid[, i], X_resid[, j], method = "mom")
    tibble(
      Pair = paste(cn[i], "/", cn[j]),
      k40  = round(kap$k40, 2),
      k31  = round(kap$k31, 2),
      k22  = round(kap$k22, 2),
      k13  = round(kap$k13, 2),
      k04  = round(kap$k04, 2)
    )
  })
}

fredmd_omega_check <- function(X_mat, X_seg) {
  n  <- nrow(X_mat)
  cn <- colnames(X_mat)
  ece_omega <- ece.complexity(X_mat) |> round(6)
  rownames(ece_omega) <- colnames(ece_omega) <- cn

  seg_omega <- matrix(0, ncol(X_mat), ncol(X_mat), dimnames = list(cn, cn))
  for (i in seq_len(ncol(X_mat))) {
    for (j in seq_len(ncol(X_mat))) {
      seg_omega[i, j] <- lag_diff(X_seg[, i], X_seg[, j], k = 1) / n
    }
  }
  list(ece = ece_omega, seg = round(seg_omega, 6))
}

fredmd_pairwise_results <- function(X_mat, X_resid) {
  ece_cor     <- ece.cor(X_mat) |> round(3)
  seg_ece_cor <- ece.cor(X_resid) |> round(3)
  dimnames(ece_cor) <- dimnames(seg_ece_cor) <- list(colnames(X_mat), colnames(X_mat))

  list(
    ece_cor      = ece_cor,
    seg_ece_cor  = seg_ece_cor,
    resid_cor    = cor(X_resid) |> round(3),
    pearson_cor  = cor(X_mat) |> round(3),
    ece_pmat     = ece_pval_null(X_mat) |> round(3),
    seg_ece_pmat = ece_pval_null(X_resid) |> round(3),
    resid_pmat   = cor_pval(X_resid) |> round(3),
    pearson_pmat = cor_pval(X_mat) |> round(3)
  )
}

# Drops Manufacturing, which is close to a linear identity (Durable + Nondurable),
# so the Diagonal test can be checked without that mechanical near-collinearity.
fredmd_no_manu <- function(X) X[, colnames(X) != "Manufacturing", drop = FALSE]

fredmd_diagonal_results <- function(X_mat, X_resid, seed = 123) {
  run_row <- function(X) {
    data.frame(
      Method = c(
        "Bootstrap Multiplier",
        "Parametric Bootstrap",
        "Parametric Bootstrap (Naive)",
        "Bartlett Test"
      ),
      `p-value` = c(
        round(ece.test(X, type = "bs.multiplier")$p.value, 3),
        round(ece.test(X, type = "bs.parametric.lag1.diag.psd")$p.value, 3),
        round(ece.test(X, type = "bs.parametric.naive")$p.value, 3),
        round(cortest.bartlett(cor(X), nrow(X))$p.value, 3)
      ),
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }
  set.seed(seed)
  raw <- run_row(X_mat)
  set.seed(seed)
  seg <- run_row(X_resid)
  list(raw = raw, seg = seg)
}

fredmd_penalty_table <- function(pen, X_seg) {
  tibble(
    Series      = colnames(X_seg),
    `pen.value` = signif(pen, 3),
    Segments    = apply(X_seg, 2, function(c) length(unique(c)))
  )
}

fredmd_segments_table <- function(X_seg, penalty_label) {
  tibble(
    Series   = colnames(X_seg),
    Penalty  = penalty_label,
    Segments = apply(X_seg, 2, function(c) length(unique(c)))
  )
}

pen_grid_raw <- 10^seq(-2, 14, length.out = 100)
pen_grid_log <- 10^seq(-8, 0, length.out = 100)
```


::: {.panel-tabset}

## Raw

`ω fitted` uses the per-series omega-matched penalty search (`pen.value` chosen so the segmentation-implied $\omega$ matches ECE's own segmentation-free estimate, `ece.complexity(x, x)`, grid-searched over `pen_grid_raw <- 10^seq(-2, 14, length.out = 100)`). `AIC` and `BIC` instead hand the penalty choice to `segment_mean()`'s own built-in criterion. All three tabs run the identical Diagnostics/Results pipeline via the same parameterized helper functions.

April 2020 is a single-month, double-digit collapse in the employment series (Manufacturing -10%, Services -14% month over month) that has no CPI counterpart of similar magnitude. The `(Pre-COVID)` tabs below rerun each of the three segmentation choices restricted to `date < 2020-01-01`, dropping the pandemic shock and every month since, to check how much of this chapter's conclusions depend on that one event.

```{R fredmd-raw-precovid-data}
#| echo: false

X_data_precovid <- X_data |> filter(date < as.Date("2020-01-01"))
X_mat_precovid  <- as.matrix(X_data_precovid[, -1])
dates_precovid  <- X_data_precovid$date
```

`r nrow(X_data_precovid)` monthly observations, `r format(min(dates_precovid))` to `r format(max(dates_precovid))`.

## Log-Transformed

```{R fredmd-log-data}
#| echo: false

X_data_log <- X_data |>
  mutate(across(-date, ~ c(NA, diff(log(.x))))) |>
  filter(!is.na(Manufacturing))

X_mat_log <- as.matrix(X_data_log[, -1])
dates_log <- X_data_log$date
```

`r nrow(X_data_log)` monthly log growth-rate observations (one fewer than the raw series, lost to differencing). Same three segmentation choices as Raw above: `ω fitted` uses `pen_grid_log <- 10^seq(-8, 0, length.out = 100)`, since log growth sits on a much smaller scale than raw levels; `AIC` and `BIC` use `segment_mean()`'s built-in criteria.

```{R fredmd-log-precovid-data}
#| echo: false

X_data_log_precovid <- X_data_log |> filter(date < as.Date("2020-01-01"))
X_mat_log_precovid  <- as.matrix(X_data_log_precovid[, -1])
dates_log_precovid  <- X_data_log_precovid$date
```

`r nrow(X_data_log_precovid)` monthly log growth-rate observations, Pre-COVID. Same rationale as Raw above: the `(Pre-COVID)` tabs drop the pandemic shock and every month since (`date < 2020-01-01`).

::: {.panel-tabset}


### ω fitted

```{R fredmd-log-omegafit-fit}
#| echo: false

fit_log_omegafit  <- fredmd_fit_segmentation(X_mat_log, pen_grid_log)
X_seg_log_omegafit   <- fit_log_omegafit$X_seg
X_resid_log_omegafit <- X_mat_log - X_seg_log_omegafit
```

```{R fredmd-log-omegafit-penalty-table}
#| echo: false

kable(fredmd_penalty_table(fit_log_omegafit$pen, X_seg_log_omegafit), align = c("l", "c", "c")) |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

